---
title: 'buildMetachronogram'
description: 'Build a metachronogram by grafting dated subtrees onto a backbone chronogram'
toc: true
toc-depth: 3
---


```{r}
#| eval: false
catGenes::buildMetachronogram()
```

### Description

Builds a large, composite time-calibrated phylogeny (a
"metachronogram", sensu Ringelberg et al.) by grafting one or more densely
sampled, ultrametric subtrees onto specified clades of a backbone
chronogram, replacing each targeted clade with the corresponding subtree
rescaled to exactly the age of the clade it replaces. This lets you
combine phylogenetic datasets generated at different taxonomic scales or
from different sequencing efforts (e.g. grafting densely sampled,
Sanger-sequenced genus-level trees onto a sparser, genome-scale backbone)
into a single time-scaled tree, while keeping every untouched part of the
backbone exactly as it was.

### Details

For each graft, the clade defined by `mrca` is located in the
backbone and its age (time before the present, assuming the backbone tips
are all at time 0) is taken as the target age. The replacement subtree is
rescaled proportionally so that its own root height exactly equals that
target age, and is then grafted in at precisely the point the original
clade occupied, preserving the stem branch leading to it. The rest of the
backbone — including branch lengths and node ages outside the replaced
clade — is left unchanged.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| backbone | An ultrametric `phylo` tree, or a `multiPhylo` object (e.g. a posterior sample of backbone trees), onto which the subtrees in `grafts` will be grafted. |
| grafts | A list of grafts to apply, in order. Each element is itself a list with two components: `mrca`, a vector of two or more tip labels whose most recent common ancestor in the (current state of the) backbone defines the clade to be replaced; and `subtree`, the ultrametric replacement `phylo` tree (or a `multiPhylo` of the same length as `backbone`, for grafting a matching posterior subtree sample onto each backbone tree). Grafts are applied in the order given, so for hierarchical grafting (grafting a subtree inside a clade that was itself just grafted in), list the least nested graft first. |
| verbose | Logical, if `FALSE`, a message showing each graft as it is applied will not be printed in the console. |
| save | Logical, if `FALSE` the resulting metachronogram(s) are returned as an R object but not saved to disk. |
| dir | The path to the directory where the metachronogram should be saved. The default is to create a directory named **RESULTS_buildMetachronogram** and save the tree within a subfolder named after the current date. |
| filename | Name (without extension) of the saved Newick tree file. |

### Value

A `phylo` object (if `backbone` is a single tree) or a
`multiPhylo` object (if `backbone` is a `multiPhylo`), with
every requested graft applied.

### Examples

```r
library(catGenes)

# single backbone tree, single graft
metatree <- buildMetachronogram(
  backbone = my_backbone_tree,
  grafts = list(
    list(mrca = c("Genus_speciesA", "Genus_speciesB"),
        subtree = my_genus_level_tree)
  )
)

# posterior sample of backbone trees, two grafts applied to every tree,
# each paired with its own posterior sample of the replacement subtree
metatrees <- buildMetachronogram(
  backbone = my_backbone_posterior,
  grafts = list(
    list(mrca = c("Genus1_speciesA", "Genus1_speciesB"),
        subtree = genus1_posterior),
    list(mrca = c("Genus2_speciesA", "Genus2_speciesB"),
        subtree = genus2_posterior)
  ),
  dir = "RESULTS_buildMetachronogram"
)
```
